name: Retirement Visa (Retired in Nigeria / Retiree from Abroad)

requirements.blocker_text: Retired in Nigeria after at least 20 years of service, having previously held temporary residency there.
Sufficient financial resources (pension, annuity, savings) to relocate to Nigeria as a retiree without engaging in paid work.

outcome.duration_length: N5A (retired in Nigeria): indefinite, no expiry, functions as full permanent residence; N5B (retiree from abroad): 2-year renewable permit

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) -- Retirement Visa N5A (Retired in Nigeria): foreign retirees 65+, retired in Nigeria after 20+ years of service, requires prior temporary residency, retirement income proof, medical insurance; indefinite residence, functions as permanent residence permit

Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) -- Nigerian Visa categories, Retirement Visa (Retiree from Abroad): allows retirees to live in Nigeria without engaging in paid work, requires sufficient financial resources and local accommodation, renewal requires updated income stability proof

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Nigeria). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- both sources tier-1. STRUCTURAL NOTE: N5A (retired-in-Nigeria) has a genuinely unusual precondition -- it requires the applicant to have ALREADY held temporary residency and worked/served in Nigeria for 20+ years before retiring there, making it functionally a capstone status for long-term prior residents rather than an entry route for someone retiring to Nigeria fresh. N5B (retiree-from-abroad) is the actual entry route for a new retiree relocating to Nigeria, but is only 2-year renewable, not indefinite, unlike N5A. Both are modeled as requirement groups within one file since they share the 'settled/retirement' purpose despite this asymmetry. No specific minimum income/pension threshold figure was found for either group at tier-1.
